title: The Personal Auto Policy
summary: Ride along through Rosa's year with her new car: the 2018 Personal Auto Policy part by part, Michigan's collision choices and the key endorsements.
objectives: Name the six parts of the Personal Auto Policy in order
Recall Part A's insureds, supplementary payments and the ride-share exclusion
Sort collision from other than collision, and pick among Michigan's collision types
Apply the new-car reporting windows and explain what the key endorsements do

scenes.title: Rosa hits the road: the Personal Auto Policy
scenes.subtitle: Parts A to F of the 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy (PP 00 01 09 18), and the Michigan rules that change it

beats.text: Meet Rosa. She just bought a new car in Lansing, insured with the 2018 Personal Auto Policy.
beats.say: Meet Rosa. She just bought a new car in Lansing, insured with the twenty eighteen Personal Auto Policy.

beats.text: This year, that car meets a deer, a thief and a hit-and-run driver. Buckle up.
beats.say: This year, that car meets a deer, a thief and a hit-and-run driver. Buckle up.

Part C Uninsured Motorists, Part D Damage to Your Auto
Part E Duties After an Accident or Loss, Part F General Provisions

scenes.title: Part D: Rosa's own car
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D, Insuring Agreement B; memory hook mn_auto-23; confusion pair cp_personal-13
scenes.plain: Collision: your car rolls over or hits a vehicle or object. Other than collision (OTC): direct, accidental loss from other causes, like fire or theft.
scenes.example: A deer leaps in front of Rosa's car near Lansing, and she hits it. Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer (or a bird) is other than collision.
scenes.exam: Swerve into a tree instead: collision. Glass broken in a collision: collision, if you choose. OTC is commonly called comprehensive.

beats.text: First, her car: Part D. Collision is the upset of the car, or its impact with another vehicle or object.
beats.say: First, her car: Part D. Collision is the upset of the car, or its impact with another vehicle or object.

beats.text: Other than collision, or OTC, covers perils like fire, theft, windstorm, hail, flood, vandalism and falling objects.
beats.say: Other than collision, or O T C, covers perils like fire, theft, windstorm, hail, flood, vandalism and falling objects.

beats.text: And Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer is other than collision.
beats.say: And Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer is other than collision.

beats.text: Swerve into a tree? Collision. Glass broken in a collision can count as collision, at Rosa's option.
beats.say: Swerve into a tree? Collision. Glass broken in a collision can count as collision, at Rosa's option.

scenes.title: Collision or OTC?
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D, Insuring Agreement B; confusion pair cp_personal-13; question auto-055

cards.text: Rosa hits a deer on a dark road outside Lansing.
cards.why: Contact with a bird or animal is other than collision. Bambi is not a collision.

cards.text: She swerves to miss a deer and hits a tree instead.
cards.why: The car's impact with an object, the tree, is collision.

cards.text: Her car rolls over on an icy curve without hitting anything.
cards.why: Upset of the auto is collision.

cards.text: Hail dents the hood and roof.
cards.why: Hail is listed as other than collision.

cards.text: A tree limb falls on her parked car during a storm.
cards.why: Falling objects are other than collision.

cards.text: She backs into a parked car at the grocery store.
cards.why: Impact with another vehicle is collision.

beats.text: Your turn. Collision, or other than collision?
beats.say: Your turn. Collision, or other than collision?

reveal.text: Rolled over, or hit a vehicle or object? Collision. An animal, weather, a falling object, fire or theft? Other than collision.
reveal.say: Rolled over, or hit a vehicle or object? Collision. An animal, weather, a falling object, fire or theft? Other than collision.

scenes.title: In Michigan: three kinds of collision
scenes.src: MCL 500.3037(1),(2),(8)(b); DIFS FIS-PUB 0200 (via confusion pair cp_personal-14); question auto-048

beats.text: In Michigan, insurers must offer two kinds of collision at a first private passenger car application. Substantially at fault means over 50% of the cause.
beats.say: In Michigan, insurers must offer two kinds of collision at a first private passenger car application. Substantially at fault means over fifty percent of the cause.

beats.text: Limited has no deductible, but pays only if the driver wasn't substantially at fault.
beats.say: Limited has no deductible, but pays only if the driver wasn't substantially at fault.

beats.text: Broad form pays regardless of fault, and waives the deductible if the driver wasn't substantially at fault.
beats.say: Broad form pays regardless of fault, and waives the deductible if the driver wasn't substantially at fault.

beats.text: Standard may also be offered: it pays regardless of fault, and you pay the deductible either way.
beats.say: Standard may also be offered: it pays regardless of fault, and you pay the deductible either way.

scenes.title: Rosa's call: which Michigan collision?
scenes.src: MCL 500.3037(1),(2),(8)(b); DIFS FIS-PUB 0200 (via confusion pair cp_personal-14)

draw.text: Fix it even if it's my fault!

beats.text: Fix my car even if it's my fault. Not my fault? No deductible. Which one, Dana?
beats.say: Fix my car even if it's my fault. Not my fault? No deductible. Which one, Dana?

options.label: Limited: no deductible!
options.fail: In Michigan, limited pays only if the driver was not substantially at fault. Rosa was 70% at fault, more than 50%, so it pays nothing.

beats.text: Months later, Rosa is 70% at fault in a crash. Limited pays nothing for her car.
beats.say: Months later, Rosa is seventy percent at fault in a crash. Limited pays nothing for her car.

options.label: Standard: pays no matter whose fault
options.fail: In Michigan, standard collision pays regardless of fault, but the driver pays the deductible either way, even with no fault at all.

beats.text: A driver runs a red light and hits Rosa. Not her fault, but standard collision still subtracts her deductible.
beats.say: A driver runs a red light and hits Rosa. Not her fault, but standard collision still subtracts her deductible.

options.label: Broad form
options.win: In Michigan, broad form pays regardless of fault, and waives the deductible when the driver was not substantially at fault.

beats.text: Broad form it is: paid regardless of fault, and no deductible when she's not substantially at fault.
beats.say: Broad form it is: paid regardless of fault, and no deductible when she's not substantially at fault.

draw.text: Any fault: pays. Not substantially at fault: no deductible

reveal.text: She adds other than collision coverage too.
reveal.say: She adds other than collision coverage too.

scenes.title: Part D bonus: a ride while the car is gone
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D, Transportation Expenses; memory hook mn_auto-22; question auto-056

draw.text: Other losses: car out of use more than

beats.text: Smart move. In October, a thief steals Rosa's car.
beats.say: Smart move. In October, a thief steals Rosa's car.

beats.text: My car! It was right here!
beats.say: My car! It was right here!

beats.text: With other than collision, Part D also pays transportation expenses, no deductible.
beats.say: With other than collision, Part D also pays transportation expenses, no deductible.

beats.text: Under the 2018 form: up to $30 a day, $900 max. Thirty times thirty is nine hundred, but that's a dollar cap, not a 30-day limit.
beats.say: Under the twenty eighteen form: up to thirty dollars a day, nine hundred dollars max. Thirty times thirty is nine hundred, but that's a dollar cap, not a thirty-day limit.

beats.text: After a total theft, payment starts after 48 hours. Other losses need the car out of use more than 24 hours.
beats.say: After a total theft, payment starts after forty-eight hours. Other losses need the car out of use more than twenty-four hours.

beats.text: A week later, police find her car.
beats.say: A week later, police find her car.

scenes.title: Part A: liability, plus extras on top
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A: Insuring Agreement, Supplementary Payments; cp_personal-12; question auto-052
scenes.plain: Extra costs Part A pays on top of the liability limit, like bail bonds, or earnings lost attending hearings or trials at the insurer's request.
scenes.example: Sued after a Toledo, Ohio crash, Rosa attends trial at the insurer's request. Her lost earnings: paid, up to $250 a day.
scenes.exam: 2018 form: bail bonds up to $250, lost earnings up to $250 a day. Defense costs: also on top of the limit.

beats.text: Part A, liability, pays for injuries and damage Rosa is legally responsible for. It covers her or a family member in any auto, and anyone using her covered auto.
beats.say: Part A, liability, pays for injuries and damage Rosa is legally responsible for. It covers her or a family member in any auto, and anyone using her covered auto.

beats.text: In Toledo, Ohio, she rear-ends a car and is sued. Her defense is paid on top of the limit, until it's used up.
beats.say: In Toledo, Ohio, she rear-ends a car and is sued. Her defense is paid on top of the limit, until it's used up.

beats.text: Supplementary payments are extra too. Under the 2018 form: bail bonds up to $250. Lost earnings for hearings or trials at the insurer's request: up to $250 a day.
beats.say: Supplementary payments are extra too. Under the twenty eighteen form: bail bonds up to two hundred fifty dollars. Lost earnings for hearings or trials at the insurer's request: up to two hundred fifty dollars a day.

scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A, Exclusion A.5; question auto-053

draw.text: How can my car pay for its gas?

beats.say: Gas isn't cheap. Rosa wants her car to help pay its way. Which plan keeps her liability coverage?

options.label: Turn on a ride-share app during her commute
options.fail: Part A excludes public or livery use, including any time logged into a ride-share app as a driver, even with no rider yet.

beats.text: She's logged in on her commute, no rider yet, when, bump, a fender bender. Excluded: time logged in as a driver counts.
beats.say: She's logged in on her commute, no rider yet, when, bump, a fender bender. Excluded: time logged in as a driver counts.

options.label: Split gas costs in a coworker car pool
options.win: The livery exclusion doesn't apply to share-the-expense car pools, or to volunteer or charitable use.

beats.text: Her coworkers chip in for gas. A share-the-expense car pool isn't excluded, so Part A applies.
beats.say: Her coworkers chip in for gas. A share-the-expense car pool isn't excluded, so Part A applies.

reveal.text: Time logged into a ride-share app as a driver is excluded, rider or not. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer driving aren't.
reveal.say: Time logged into a ride-share app as a driver is excluded, rider or not. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer driving aren't.

scenes.title: Parts B and C: help for injuries
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part B A-B; Part C A, C; DIFS auto FAQ; Rory v Continental (2005); questions auto-049, auto-054

draw.text: Medical and funeral costs, services within 3 years
Rosa and family members, even on foot, plus anyone in her covered auto
Michigan: UM and UIM optional (DIFS; Supreme Court for UM)

beats.text: Part B, medical payments, pays medical and funeral costs for services within 3 years of the accident.
beats.say: Part B, medical payments, pays medical and funeral costs for services within three years of the accident.

beats.text: It covers Rosa and her family members, even as pedestrians, and anyone in her covered auto.
beats.say: It covers Rosa and her family members, even as pedestrians, and anyone in her covered auto.

beats.text: Part C, uninsured motorists, pays injury damages an uninsured driver owes her. Hit-and-runs and insolvent insurers count. Government-owned vehicles don't.
beats.say: Part C, uninsured motorists, pays injury damages an uninsured driver owes her. Hit-and-runs and insolvent insurers count. Government-owned vehicles don't.

beats.text: In Michigan, DIFS lists UM and UIM, underinsured motorists, as optional. Rosa bought both.
beats.say: In Michigan, D I F S lists U M and U I M, underinsured motorists, as optional. Rosa bought both.

scenes.title: Part E: Rosa's duties after a hit-and-run
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part E (opening), A-C; Part C, C; DIFS auto FAQ; questions auto-gap-05, auto-gap-06

draw.text: Prompt notice. Cooperate. Legal papers. Exams. Records. Proof of loss.
A failure that prejudices the insurer? No duty to provide coverage

beats.text: One night, an unknown driver rear-ends Rosa's car and speeds off. She's seriously hurt, so she makes an uninsured motorists claim.
beats.say: One night, an unknown driver rear-ends Rosa's car and speeds off. She's seriously hurt, so she makes an uninsured motorists claim.

beats.text: They just drove off!
beats.say: They just drove off!

beats.text: For a hit-and-run, Part E says: promptly notify the police. Rosa does.
beats.say: For a hit-and-run, Part E says: promptly notify the police. Rosa does.

beats.text: Plus the usual duties: prompt notice to the insurer, cooperation, legal papers, exams, records and proof of loss.
beats.say: Plus the usual duties: prompt notice to the insurer, cooperation, legal papers, exams, records and proof of loss.

beats.text: If skipping a duty hurts, or prejudices, the insurer, it has no duty to provide coverage.
beats.say: If skipping a duty hurts, or prejudices, the insurer, it has no duty to provide coverage.

scenes.title: Sam's call: when to ask for collision?
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Definitions K.2; memory hook mn_auto-21; question auto-051

draw.text: I haven't called the insurer yet!

beats.text: Sam buys a second car Monday. Wednesday, before calling, he bumps the new car into a stop sign.
beats.say: Sam buys a second car Monday. Wednesday, before calling, he bumps the new car into a stop sign.

beats.text: His 2018 policy gives a new car 14 days to ask for collision. Only 4 if no car on the policy has it. None of Sam's do.
beats.say: His twenty eighteen policy gives a new car fourteen days to ask for collision. Only four if no car on the policy has it. None of Sam's do.

beats.text: When should he ask?
beats.say: When should he ask?

options.label: Next week. He has 14 days!
options.fail: If no declared auto has collision, ask within 4 days. Ask late, and coverage begins only when you ask.

beats.text: Ten days later, he calls. Too late: coverage starts only when he asks.
beats.say: Ten days later, he calls. Too late: coverage starts only when he asks.

draw.text: The dent came before coverage began

options.label: Thursday, within 4 days
options.win: No declared auto with collision: ask within 4 days. A $500 deductible applies to a loss before you asked.

beats.text: Thursday is within 4 days, so he's covered from the day he became the owner, minus a deductible of $500.
beats.say: Thursday is within four days, so he's covered from the day he became the owner, minus a deductible of five hundred dollars.

reveal.text: A fortnight for most, four days for first-timers with no collision yet. Miss the window, and coverage starts only when you ask.
reveal.say: A fortnight for most, four days for first-timers with no collision yet. Miss the window, and coverage starts only when you ask.

scenes.title: Endorsements: filling the gaps
scenes.src: PP 03 23 (FC&S summary; form not read); PP 03 06 01 05; PP 00 01 09 18 Part A Excl. B; DIFS Bulletin 96-02; MCL 500.3109(3)

spots.label: Motorcycle
spots.text: Part A excludes vehicles with fewer than 4 wheels or built mainly for off-road use. Miscellaneous Type Vehicle removes that for listed vehicles.

spots.label: Miscellaneous Type Vehicle
spots.text: This endorsement typically covers motor homes, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, dune buggies and golf carts.

spots.label: Snowmobile
spots.text: Not on the Miscellaneous Type Vehicle endorsement: snowmobiles use a separate endorsement.

spots.label: A borrowed golf cart
spots.text: The fewer-than-4-wheels or off-road exclusion has exceptions: trailers, non-owned golf carts, and use in a medical emergency.

spots.label: Extended Non-Owned
spots.text: Part A excludes vehicles furnished or available for your regular use. This removes that for liability, and med pay if bought. Michigan: residual liability only.

spots.label: Michigan PIP and PPI
spots.text: The base form has no PIP or PPI, so Michigan endorsements add them. A PIP deductible applies only to the named insured, spouse and resident relatives.

beats.text: December: Rosa gets a company car, and Gramps buys a motor home.
beats.say: December: Rosa gets a company car, and Gramps buys a motor home.

beats.text: Endorsements, forms that change or add to the policy, fill the gaps. Tap the glowing spots.
beats.say: Endorsements, forms that change or add to the policy, fill the gaps. Tap the glowing spots.

reveal.text: So Gramps' motor home typically fits Miscellaneous Type Vehicle. Rosa's company car fits Extended Non-Owned.
reveal.say: So Gramps' motor home typically fits Miscellaneous Type Vehicle. Rosa's company car fits Extended Non-Owned.

reveal.text: But in Michigan, DIFS says extended non-owned and named non-owner endorsements give residual liability only, for harm you cause others.
reveal.say: But in Michigan, D I F S says extended non-owned and named non-owner endorsements give residual liability only, for harm you cause others.

scenes.q: Rosa's Michigan policy adds an extended non-owned endorsement for her company car. According to DIFS, it gives her:
choices: PIP, PPI and residual liability for the whole household
Residual liability only, for the named person and spouse
scenes.why: DIFS Bulletin 96-02: only residual liability, only for the named person and spouse. No PIP, PPI or physical damage, so it doesn't meet no-fault requirements.

beats.text: Quick check: what does Rosa's endorsement give her?
beats.say: Quick check: what does Rosa's endorsement give her?

reveal.text: Residual liability only, and only for the named person and spouse. No PIP, PPI or physical damage.
reveal.say: Residual liability only, and only for the named person and spouse. No P I P, P P I or physical damage.

beats.text: In Michigan, limited collision pays only if the driver wasn't substantially at fault. Under the 2018 form, no collision on the policy? A new car gets four days.
